title.label: This transition to the new format is beyond challenging

content.label: I wrote a Caring Bridge post this evening and posted it. Then I shared it with about a dozen friends who aren’t able to follow it online with a link sent via text. Some were apparently able to access it, but others weren’t. Ditto for those who read our posts online. We heard from a couple of people, but even my own husband just got a blank screen when he tried to read the post on Caring Bridge. At one point I finally realized that the instructions for sharing posts could only be followed on my computer, not on the mobile app. So I copied the link as instructed, but ran aground from not knowing how to send the copied link from my computer to my phone to send in a text message. This transition to the new Caring Bridge has meant running into one scary wall after another. It’s kind of sad that you aren’t able to staff a “help” phone line. That would help a great deal. Thanks for the wonderful service you have provided for us across these last years of our cancer journey. But I may have to look for some kind of alternative because our lives are stressful enough without the daily drama of wondering what the next challenge will be

When I try to create a post in the app, the app opens a new editor page, but without a keyboard. I am unable to either type or dictate anything and have to go to my laptop to create a post via the web browser. This makes the app of very limited use.

There are so many glitches with this app. I can’t tell you how many times I’ve typed out a whole post and it gets lost because the app force closes or does not save the draft. Also, they deceivingly advertise “tributes” as a way to directly support the family in need, but instead it is a donation to their own app. I have had several family members think they were donating money to us when in reality it goes to the app. The language must be changed to clarify this distinction. It is disgusting, horrible behavior to pray on people in that manner. This cannot be compliant with standards as a 501(c)(3). We started this page because some folks do not have Facebook or other social media, but we sincerely regret this decision and wished we had just made a Facebook page instead.
Hate the updates that were made to the app. Hard to find the sites I watch. Can’t delete a search/site.

I’ve authored and co-authored several CaringBridge sites over the years. I have appreciated the relative ease of creating, updating and otherwise modifying sites - until earlier this year. Don’t know what happened to blow CaringBridge out of the water a few months ago, and the complete lack of communication about it was baffling. I’d still appreciate something more than “we’re working hard.”

While there’s been progress in recent months, the site still lacks much of its previous usability. As an author, I find it clumsy, difficult, and frustrating to use. More importantly, large numbers of my sister’s supporters and readers have stopped using it, and that is a very great loss.

Are there plans to restore more functionality? Will CaringBridge communicate anything of substance that might help its users? Is anyone paying attention to feedback from the community of users? I hope so.

Thanks for your time and attention.

Dear Staff of CaringBridge, I can’t thank you enough for having this website (app) available for our family who has now used it for two of our children. The changes that have been made in the last several months have been incredibly disappointing, however. Many of my pictures have not been restored where I can see them. It’s also not possible to see the captions that I put below them to help describe each of the pictures. It also doesn’t look like I am able to print a copy of our daughter’s cancer journey. This is incredibly hard to not be able to have this as a keepsake for her. One suggestion that I have with the visitors page is to be able to see when they most recently signed in (as before) and also to have a separate option of putting those visitors in alphabetical order. And the “well wishes” that people have given… Where did they go? Going back and seeing people’s words of encouragement continue to give us strength for the journey. Lastly, I have noticed our friends have given hearts to either pictures or updates, but I am not able to see who has responded in that way. Once again, we are very thankful for this website (app), but in its original form. Is there any way to go back?

title.label: From great app to awful app

content.label:
I’ve been using this app and website for about 1 1/2 years to keep friends and family informed. With the platform update the app no longer gives allows you to see who reacted to a journal entry or how they reacted. It looks like they finally fixed the issue with the visitor list not closing when pressing “Done”. 

A new look is one thing, but not at the regression of features, please. This platform update went out without usability testing, has taken months to fix and still has bugs. 

I appreciate and am grateful for CaringBridge, but I don’t understand going from a great platform and user experience to a poor performing, poorly executed design. It makes me sad for the $$ spent on it.
The app is not what it used to be. It is not nearly as good as it was.
